done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves, so a proof list never names a test that did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. The results hook truncates the shared results file whenever pytest starts. A documented `fast_test` command such as `pytest tests/unit && pytest tests/integration` runs both suites, but the second invocation erases the first suite's results. Close then marks named unit tests `not run` even though it ran them. The command-level proof uses one pytest invocation, so it does not cover this case.
findings.title: Close loses results from the first pytest run in a compound test command

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The worker instructions explicitly allow a test file as proof. If `tests/test_feature.py` contains two cases and Close runs only one passing case, `_ran` matches the file to that case and this line publishes the whole file as `passed`. The list therefore credits a file containing an unrun case without showing that the case was not run. The named command test covers case-level node IDs but no file-level proof.
findings.title: Close marks a partly run test file as passed

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 1-2, reversible): after the area answer in round 3, a new finding in review.py holds work only at Harm 3 or more (approved scoring rule). Follow-ups: match a named test by its exact path from the repo root, not a path suffix (rare: two test files with the same nested tail); parameter ids with spaces (Gain 2, lived with).

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
